title: Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule Act
official_title: To provide for the creation of a congressional time capsule in commemoration of the semiquincentennial of the United States, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-79 (PL 119-79) on February 18, 2026. Introduced by Sen. Thomas Tillis (R-NC); directing the Architect of the Capitol to create and bury a commemorative time capsule is a narrow ceremonial measure that drew no recorded opposition, passing the Senate and House before being signed.
summary: Directs the Architect of the Capitol to build a congressional time capsule marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. The capsule is to be sealed and buried in the Capitol Visitor Center, then opened on July 4, 2276.
brief: Creates a congressional time capsule to be sealed and buried at the Capitol and unsealed in 2276.

top_lines.headline: Congressional Time Capsule
subs: Architect of the Capitol builds the capsule
Capsule limited to 50 in. wide, 32 in. deep, 48 in. high
Sealed and buried in the Capitol Visitor Center

top_lines.headline: Contents and Materials
subs: Congressional leadership offices jointly choose contents
Must include one joint letter from those offices
Items must use low-degradation materials such as metal or archival paper

top_lines.headline: Sealing and Unsealing
subs: Prepared and buried on or before July 4, 2026
Presented to the 244th Congress on unsealing

items.main: Names the Act the “Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Directs the Architect of the Capitol to create, seal, and bury a congressional time capsule, with contents chosen by congressional leadership.
items.detail: The Speaker, House Minority Leader, Senate Majority Leader, and Senate Minority Leader jointly determine the contents, which must include a single joint letter from those offices and may include other items they agree on. Items must be made of low-degradation materials such as metal or archival paper, and the capsule may be no more than 50 inches wide, 32 inches deep, and 48 inches high. The Architect prepares it to be sealed and buried in the Capitol Visitor Center on or before July 4, 2026, with the approval of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration and the House Committee on House Administration, installs a plaque, and the capsule stays sealed until July 4, 2276, when it is presented to the 244th Congress.

gaps: The Act sets the burial to coincide with a time capsule buried at Independence Mall in Philadelphia but does not address what happens if the July 4, 2026 deadline is not met.
The Act specifies the maximum capsule dimensions and material requirements but does not name a funding source for building, sealing, or installing the capsule and its plaque.
The Act directs that the capsule be presented to the 244th Congress in 2276 but does not specify how or where it is to be stored or safeguarded during the intervening 250 years.

added: Creates the Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule, built by the Architect of the Capitol and buried in the Capitol Visitor Center
Requires a single joint letter from the four congressional leadership offices to be included in the capsule
Requires a plaque describing the capsule to be installed
